predicates.description: The speaker asks the assistant to produce or work on content that is delivered inside this conversation: create (plan, draft, propose, suggest, list, outline), revise (change, update, adapt, make it X), explain or evaluate (why does it work, is it good, is anything worth changing), describe, compare, or summarize a plan, draft, idea, list, or the conversation itself -- whether phrased as a command, a polite request, or a question such as 'what X would work for Y?'. The result is words in this chat, so no tool, app, or outside system is needed: drafting an email, making a checklist to copy, or suggesting calendar times is this predicate. Use action_request instead only when the speaker wants something changed outside this conversation (send, order, book, buy, create an event or reminder in an app, export a file, edit an online record). Use one frame per requested operation.

predicates.description: The speaker asks the assistant to cause an effect outside this conversation: send, order, book, buy, check an external account, create or change a reminder, event, file, setting, or record in an app or service, or delete something -- including polite forms such as 'can you ...' and 'I need you to ...'. Content the assistant writes in the chat (a plan, draft, list, summary, explanation) is collaborative_content_request, never this. Use one frame per requested action.
